scope.population: 2,480,267 rows of the trade-print panel reduced to per-wallet realized PnL against per-wallet mean markout; a wallet enters on one finite markout trade, with no fill floor applied
scope.window: 10 days present in the input, day-of-month 4-13; the calendar dates of the window are declared by its producer, build_quickwin_markouts.py

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

_meta.object: M4 realized-PnL vs price-markout cross-method validation
_meta.headline: Spearman(realized_pnl, mean mo10) per wallet, per coin + pooled
_meta.realized_pnl_def: sum closed_pnl over wallet's CLOSE trades, close set = is_open == 0 (the COMPLETE close/reduce set, including the dir_code == -1 genuine closes); NOT the literal dir_code in {2,3}

close_set_bookkeeping.note: the dir_code == -1 closes are real closes the literal {2,3} set drops; they sum closed_pnl ~ -46,889.64 and flip the BTC total

_meta.markout_tox_def: mean mo10 over wallet's finite-markout trades (bps)
_meta.claim: a wallet toxic by price-markout should ALSO realize profit; two methodologically distinct measures with no shared reference-price model agreeing in direction hardens the toxicity label (closedPnl and mo10 share the same fills, so this is a cross-method check, not two independent samples)
_meta.rank_floor_note: wallets enter on one finite markout trade, not on the declared 50-fill floor: the statistic is a cross-method agreement over the whole wallet population, and flooring it would restate the population being validated

BTC.effect_size_note: rho is small in magnitude (~0.03); the floored permutation p reflects large N, NOT a strong agreement. Two methodologically distinct measures agree in DIRECTION, weakly.
BTC.interpretation: positive rho => wallets that look toxic by price-markout also tend to realize profit; two methodologically distinct toxicity measures (no shared reference-price model) agree in direction, weakly

procedure.method: permutation p = (draws at least as extreme + 1) / (usable draws + 1); the observed labelling counts as one draw of its own null, so p is floored at 1/(usable + 1) and is never zero
